note: Hand-verified expectations, one row per word (SPEC Principle 5, 2026-09-05). Each row is a fact read off the extracts at kaikki 2026-09-01 and the curation tables, never a hope: kind is morphs, decomposed, single, rowonly or none; parts are the ordered chip forms as the card shows them. The build scores itself against these rows on every run and fails under the score in gold-score.json. A field report becomes a row here before it becomes a fix.

rows.why: bor+ la componens; compōnēns is a participle page stepping to compōnō, whose ety reads con- + pōnō
bor la-med manūscrīptum, an inflection of manūscrīptus, whose prose reads manu (ablative of manus) + scriptus (past participle of scribere)
der la absolūtus, the participle of absolvō, whose etymon reads ab- + solvō
der la absolūtiōnem, an inflection of absolūtiō = absolvō + -tiō; absolvō is no anchor and flattens to ab- + solvō
der la pressāre, the infinitive of pressō, whose ety reads premō + -tō
der la impressus, the participle of imprimō, whose etymon reads in- + premō
der grc σύστημα = σῠνῐ́στημῐ + -μᾰ (length marks stripped); συνίστημι = συν- + ἵστημι and is no anchor
der grc περίοδος; the Greek page splits it as περῐ́ + ὁδός, the preposition περί through the length-mark rule
bor+ la idea, der grc ἰδέα: the deepest run is Greek and ἰδέα has no split (its etymon names one parent)
der la soccus, der grc σύκχος: σύκχος is an alternative-form page, no node, so the Latin run is the deepest that exists
der la cūriōsus; the Latin page records a back-formation from incūriōsus, and SOURCE_SPLITS carries the standard analysis cūra + -ōsus
der la dēpōnēns steps to dēpōnō (LEMMA_STEPS and the participle step agree), whose ety reads dē- + pōnō
bor la haesitātiōnem steps to haesitātiō = haesitō + -tiō; haesitō is an anchor (hesitance and hesitation both reach it) and carries haereō + -titō on its card
der la accessus, whose noun entry reads accēdō + -tus; accēdō is an anchor
der la concēdō, whose ety reads con- + cēdō
der la territōrium = terra + -tōrium
der la-lat rememorari steps to rememoror, which ROOT_ALIASES folds onto la:memor; the page says only From memoror
der la memoria = memor + -ia
FORCED_SPLITS; the extract analyses it as Latin subterrāneus + -an
af en Korea + -an; Korea is a proper noun with no card, so its chip is inert
inh enm sky, der non ský (cloud): the deepest attested origin is Old Norse, a row-only language
der la cava (cavity); the page has a hollow noun and a jackdaw noun, and the attaching gloss picks the hollow
inh ang piper, der la piper: the Latin run is the deepest root language and piper has no split
der la mea domina, a two-word lemma Wiktionary never wrote; the misses report says so
inh enm knowen, inh ang cnāwan; Latin cognoscō sits only in a cog template under the Cognates heading, so no classical row (review finding 1)
inh enm riden, inh ang rīdan; Greek ὀρίνω is a cog template in the cognate list, so no classical row (review finding 1)
inh enm streight, der ang streċċan; Latin strictus is a noncog mention in the conflation note about strait, so no classical row (review finding 1)
der la iūstus; the Latin page reads surf iūs + -tus, and the iūs card follows the law entry: justice glosses iūs as right, just as law, right (review finding 2)
der la computō = con- + putō; the putō page has one lemma entry, so the chip names it whatever the card gloss says (review finding 2)
der la collēgium = collēga + -ium; collēga is an anchor carrying con- + legō, and the legō card follows the gather entry (review finding 2)
der la collecta, whose page steps through collēctus to colligō = com- + legō (to gather), flattened to the page's own parts (review finding 2)
der la-lat lectura, der la lectus (past participle of legō): the run settles on legō, whose gather entry has no split (review finding 2)
der la dēcīdere, infinitive of dēcīdō (cut off, decide), from dē + caedō: the page dēcidō has two entries and the cut entry wins on the form, the gloss and the named part (review finding 3)
der la accidēns, participle of accidō (happen) = ad + cadō: the fall entry of accido wins on the gloss and the named part cadō (review finding 3)
der la-lat captio with the verb form captiāre, a page whose only entry is the noun deception, so it is skipped; der la captō = capiō + -tō (review finding 3)
der la fundō with the form fundāre, the first-conjugation entry (to found) = fundus + -ō; the pour entry is fundere (review finding 3)
der la situs (position, place, site): the noun entry = sinō + -tus wins on the gloss over the participle (review finding 3)
der la impāctus: the noun entry (collision, hit) = impingō + -tus wins on the first definition (collision), impingō flattens to in- + pangō (review finding 3)
der la liquor (fluidity, liquidness): the noun entry = liqueō + -or wins on the gloss over the deponent verb (review finding 3)
